summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on fraud/security, regulation.

articles.title: PayPal, Venmo connect to colleges
articles.description: The peer-to-peer player and its PayPal parent have forged new ties to higher education institutions, allowing students to make payments with the P2P tool.

articles.title: Regulators pursue stablecoin rules
articles.description: Separate proposals advanced by the SEC and the FASB this week could provide the cryptocurrency sector with regulatory relief as legislation founders.

articles.title: Considering card network options
articles.description: "The real challenge for merchants is not which rail a payment uses but a lack of visibility, control, and intelligence to optimize payment flows," a fintech marketing executive writes.

articles.title: Teens targeted for scams
articles.description: It’s not just the elderly being drawn into fraud. Young people are also increasingly prey for financial crime, according to a Federal Reserve report.

articles.title: Visa, DOJ lawyers clash ahead of trial
articles.description: The government and card network are trading accusations of overly broad discovery requests and ‘gamesmanship’ in the DOJ’s debit card lawsuit.

articles.title: Stripe, OpenRouter finally strike a deal
articles.description: The payments behemoth’s acquisition of the AI spend management firm has been in the works for weeks. The reported price tag: $7.5 billion.

articles.title: Weave scooped up for $650M
articles.description: The latest purchase by Fransciso Partners adds to the private equity firm’s stockpile of payments companies, including one it bought earlier this month.

articles.title: Stripe acquisition may bolster its AI strategy
articles.description: If the company completes a prospective acquisition of OpenRouter, it will set itself up to be at the center of artificial intelligence token payments.
